answer: The wiki does not hold a single 'AI maturity framework' page — it holds a cluster of frameworks and a cross-instrument measurement comparison, tracked across one concept page, one synthesis, and one open thread. The core staged-maturity model is MIT CISR's Four Stages of AI Maturity: Experiment and prepare (28%, 2022 baseline) -> Build pilots and capabilities (34%) -> Develop AI ways of working (31%) -> Become AI future-ready (7%) [W1]. The financial inflection point sits at the Stage 2->3 transition; MIT CISR names four organizational blockers — Strategy, Systems, Synchronization, Stewardship [W1]. Four to seven other instruments measure 'maturity' differently: AI Index/McKinsey pegs 1% of C-suite executives as calling their GenAI rollout mature; MIT CISR pegs 7% at Stage 4; Cisco's 2025 readiness survey pegs 13% as ready; Werner-Le-Brun's general-transformation study finds 12% show sustained gains [W2]. Beyond staged maturity, the wiki tracks ten further organizational-AI-adoption frameworks, synthesized as mostly-complementary lenses on different decision layers: org-design (Tin Man vs Octopus), readiness (Cisco 5 Foundations), organizational learning (Augmented Learners 2x2), transformation playbook (McKinsey Rewired), firm-boundary (Nishar-Nohria), trap-escape (Bain/OpenAI), task deployment (Anand-Wu 2x2), deployment maturity (Beutler's Ask->Assist->Automate), runtime engineering (agent-harness stack), plus Carucci's cross-cutting resistance-as-data lens [W3]. The one number every instrument agrees on: adoption breadth is high (78-88%) while maturity/readiness depth clusters tightly at 7-15% across five to seven independent instruments [W4]. A documented gap: the wiki explicitly notes it does not yet cover Gartner's AI maturity model or Deloitte's State of AI in the Enterprise [W5].
